Unless otherwise stated, reactions were performed in flame-dried glassware under an argon
or nitrogen atmosphere using dry, deoxygenated solvents. Solvents were dried by passage through
an activated alumina column under argon.1 Reaction progress was monitored by thin-layer
chromatography (TLC) or Agilent 1290 UHPLC-MS. TLC was performed using E. Merck silica
gel 60 F254 precoated glass plates (0.25 mm) and visualized by UV fluorescence quenching, p-
anisaldehyde, or KMnO4 staining. Silicycle SiliaFlash® P60 Academic Silica gel (particle size
40–63 µm) was used for silica gel flash chromatography. 1H NMR spectra were recorded on
Bruker 400 MHz spectrometers and are reported relative to residual CHCl3 (δ 7.26 ppm). 13C NMR
spectra were recorded on a Bruker 400 MHz spectrometer (100 MHz) and are reported relative to
residual CDCl3 (δ 77.16 ppm).19F NMR spectra were recorded on a Varian Mercury 300 MHz
spectrometer (282 MHz). Data for 1H NMR are reported as follows: chemical shift (δ ppm)
(multiplicity, coupling constant (Hz), integration). Multiplicities are reported as follows: s =
singlet, d = doublet, t = triplet, q = quartet, p = pentet, sept = septuplet, m = multiplet, br s = broad
singlet. Data for 13C NMR, and 19F NMR are reported in terms of chemical shifts (δ ppm). IR
spectra were obtained by use of a Perkin Elmer Spectrum BXII spectrometer using thin films
deposited on NaCl plates and reported in frequency of absorption (cm–1). High resolution mass
spectra (HRMS) were obtained from the Caltech Mass Spectral Facility using either a JEOL JMS-
T2000 AccuTOF GC-Alpha time-of-flight mass spectrometer using Field Desorption (FD)
ionization (ions detected are M+•), an Agilent 6200 Series TOF with an Agilent G1978A
Multimode source in mixed ionization mode (MM: ESI-APCI), or an LC-MS using a Waters LCT
Premier XE Electrospray (ES) TOF mass spectrometer interfaced with a Waters UPLC
chromatography system (negative ion mode, ions detected are M–). The Caltech Chemistry
Division Mass Spectrometry laboratory acknowledges DOW Chemical Company (DOW Next
Generation Instrumentation Grant) and the NSF CRIF program for providing funds that enabled
Reagents were purchased from commercial sources and used as received unless otherwise

the b-keto ester in 1,4-dioxane, then adding this solution to solid lithium tert-butoxide and

glovebox, and heated at 40 °C in a heating mantle for 4 h unless otherwise noted. Reactions were
typically green at the beginning of the reaction and brown upon completion. Following reaction
completion, the reaction was quenched with sat. NaHCO3 (1 mL), extracted five times with ethyl
acetate, dried with a plug of Na2SO4, concentrated, and purified by preparative TLC.

Procedure for 1.0 mmol Scale Nickelocene-Catalyzed Amidation Reaction
In a nitrogen-filled glovebox, a 2-dram vial was charged with hydroxamic ester (1.0 mmol, 1.0
equiv). 1,4-dioxane was added (1.0 mL) followed sequentially by a stock solution of nickelocene
(0.05 mmol, 5 mol%) and phenylsilane (1.0 mmol, 1.0 equiv) in 1,4-dioxane (1.0 mL), then a stock
solution of b-keto ester (2.2 mmol, 2.2 equiv) and lithium tert-butoxide (1.5. mmol, 1.5 equiv) in
1,4-dioxane (3.0 mL). The latter solution was prepared by first preparing a solution of the b-keto
ester in 1,4-dioxane, then adding this solution to solid lithium tert-butoxide and allowing to
dissolve. The reaction vial was then sealed with a Teflon-lined cap, removed from the glovebox,
and stirred at 40 °C in a heating mantle for 20 h. Reaction was green at the beginning of the reaction
and brown upon completion. Following reaction completion as determined by TLC and LCMS,
the reaction was quenched with sat. NaHCO3 (5 mL), extracted five times with ethyl acetate, dried
with over Na2SO4, concentrated, and purified by column chromatography (30% EtOAc/hexanes)
to give the amidated product as a colorless oil (204.8 mg, 78% yield).
